rules.rule:
ProGuard/R8 configuration.

- A keep rule that is removed or narrowed breaks release-only builds: classes reached solely by reflection (Gson, Moshi, kotlinx.serialization, Retrofit, Hilt/Dagger, model classes for JSON) must stay kept. Report a removed or narrowed keep rule unless the same change also removes the reflective access.
- `-dontshrink`, `-dontobfuscate` or `-dontoptimize` disables a release safeguard; require an explicit reason in a comment.
- A blanket keep (`-keep class **`, `-keep class com.example.** { *; }`) makes shrinking pointless.
- A new `-dontwarn <package>` hides a genuinely missing dependency.
- A global option in a library module's `consumer-rules.pro` (`-dontoptimize`, `-dontshrink`, `-dontobfuscate`, a blanket `-keep class **`) applies to every app that consumes the module and turns that app's release safeguards off from outside it; AGP 9.4 already reports these as errors (`android.r8.globalOptionsInConsumerRules.disallowed`). Report it and point at the module's own rules file. Team-wide rule: report it whenever this file is reviewed, whether or not the diff touches that line - every module's consumer rules are judged, not only the module the diff touched. = high.

Scope: judge this change, not the whole file - report what the added or removed lines do. Do not flag pre-existing problems the diff does not touch, apart from the global options in a consumer rules file above.
Severity: crash, data loss or authz bypass = critical/high; contract or behaviour change = high; maintainability = medium; style or wording = low.

Gradle build script (Android).

- Dependency version that is not pinned: `-SNAPSHOT`, `+`, `latest.release`, `[1.0,)`. Require an explicit version. Ignore this when the version is not on an added or modified line.
- Team build baseline: `minSdk` must be 23 and `targetSdk` must be 36 or newer - Groovy `minSdkVersion 23` / `targetSdkVersion 36`, Kotlin DSL `minSdk = 23` / `targetSdk = 36`, or a value this file reads from the version catalog. This is a team-wide rule, not a per-change preference: report a value outside the baseline whenever this file is reviewed, whether or not the diff touches that line. `minSdk` above 23 drops devices the team still supports; `minSdk` below 23 needs a compatibility review; `targetSdk` below 36 is under the baseline the team ships against. A value outside the baseline = medium; lowering an already-valid value past the baseline = high.
- Team build baseline: the Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) must be 9.0.0 or newer. Every `com.android.*` plugin this file declares - `com.android.application`, `com.android.library`, `com.android.legacy-kapt` - carries the same baseline, whether the version is inline (`id 'com.android.application' version '9.4.0'`, `classpath 'com.android.tools.build:gradle:9.4.0'`) or resolved through a version catalog alias; an AGP below 9.0.0 does not match the Gradle 9.x wrapper baseline either. Team-wide rule: report it whenever this file is reviewed, whether or not the diff touches that line. Below the baseline = medium; lowering an already-valid version past it = high.
- Team dependency baseline: the Adjust SDK must be 5.5.0 or newer. Every `com.adjust.sdk:*` dependency this file carries - `com.adjust.sdk:adjust-android` and its companion artifacts, inline or resolved through a version catalog alias - is under that floor. Team-wide rule: report it whenever this file is reviewed, whether or not the diff touches that line. Below the baseline = medium; lowering an already-valid version past it = high.
- `compileSdk` changed: report and require the reason.
- Team release safeguard baseline: a release build type sets both `isMinifyEnabled = true` (`minifyEnabled true`) and `isShrinkResources = true` (`shrinkResources true`). Minification off ships dead code and kills shrinking, obfuscation and optimization; resource shrinking left off keeps the resources only dead code referenced. Team-wide rule: report it whenever this file is reviewed, whether or not the diff touches that line. Off, or lowered from `true` = high.
- `getDefaultProguardFile("proguard-android.txt")` for a build type with minification on: that file carries `-dontoptimize`, so R8 performs no optimization at all and the optimization percentage Play reports is 0. Require `proguard-android-optimize.txt`; a temporary `-dontoptimize` belongs in a custom rules file with a comment saying what it works around. AGP 9.4 already fails the build on this, earlier AGP versions do not. Team-wide rule: report it whenever this file is reviewed, whether or not the diff touches that line, and in every module of the project. = high.
- A release `postProcessing` block that sets `isOptimizationsEnabled`, `isObfuscationEnabled` or `isShrinkingEnabled` to `false` turns the same safeguard off; require the reason in the change. Team-wide rule: report it whenever this file is reviewed, whether or not the diff touches that line. = high.
- Signing credentials, keystore passwords or a `storeFile` outside the repository hardcoded in the script.
- Dependency scope drift: a debug-only library moved to `implementation`/`api` (it now ships in release), or a release library moved to `debugImplementation`.
- `api()` used where `implementation()` would do - `api` leaks the dependency to every consumer.
- A dependency added with no version while no BOM/platform is applied in the same file.
- A repository declared here rather than centrally in settings.gradle.
- `packagingOptions`/`packaging` that silently drops `.so` files or resources.
- `applicationId`, `versionCode` or `versionName` changed.

Scope: judge this change, not the whole file - report what the added or removed lines do. Do not flag pre-existing problems the diff does not touch, apart from the build baseline, the release safeguard baseline and the default ProGuard file baseline above.
Severity: crash, data loss or authz bypass = critical/high; contract or behaviour change = high; maintainability = medium; style or wording = low.

Gradle settings (Android).

- A repository added to `pluginManagement` or `dependencyResolutionManagement` that is not the team allowlist (google(), mavenCentral(), the company mirror). A new third-party repository is a supply-chain decision, not a build detail.
- `repositoriesMode` relaxed away from `FAIL_ON_PROJECT_REPOS`.
- A module removed from `include` - orphaned source or a deliberate split?
- A module added to `include` with no corresponding directory.
- Team build baseline: an Android Gradle Plugin version pinned here (`pluginManagement { plugins { id 'com.android.application' version '...' } }`) must be 9.0.0 or newer, the same floor as everywhere else. Team-wide rule: report it whenever this file is reviewed, whether or not the diff touches that line. Below the baseline = medium; lowering an already-valid version past it = high.

Scope: judge this change, not the whole file - report what the added or removed lines do. Do not flag pre-existing problems the diff does not touch, apart from the build baseline above.
Severity: crash, data loss or authz bypass = critical/high; contract or behaviour change = high; maintainability = medium; style or wording = low.

Gradle version catalog.

- A `[versions]` entry removed or downgraded while `[libraries]` or `[plugins]` still reference it - the build breaks or silently regresses.
- A library or plugin alias added with no matching version entry.
- Two aliases resolving to different versions of the same artifact group.
- A version that is not pinned (`-SNAPSHOT`, `+`, a dynamic range).
- A version and its alias renamed without updating the consumer, or an entry left behind under the old name.
- Team build baseline: a `minSdk` entry that is not 23, a `targetSdk` entry below 36, or the Android Gradle Plugin version entry below 9.0.0 (the alias behind `com.android.application` / `com.android.library`, commonly `agp`), or the Adjust SDK version entry below 5.5.0 (the alias behind `com.adjust.sdk:*`, commonly `adjust`), is outside the baseline the team ships against. This is a team-wide rule: report it whenever this file is reviewed, whether or not the diff touches that line. Outside the baseline = medium; a lowering of an already-valid entry past the baseline = high.

Scope: judge this change, not the whole file - report what the added or removed lines do. Do not flag pre-existing problems the diff does not touch, apart from the build baseline above.
Severity: crash, data loss or authz bypass = critical/high; contract or behaviour change = high; maintainability = medium; style or wording = low.

Gradle wrapper configuration.

- Team build baseline: the Gradle distribution this wrapper downloads must be 9.0.0 or newer - the Gradle wrapper baseline, alongside the AGP 9.0.0 baseline in the build scripts. The version is the `gradle-x.y.z` token in `distributionUrl` (`gradle-9.6.0-bin.zip` is 9.6.0, and a bare `9.0` counts as 9.0.0). This is a team-wide rule, not a per-change preference: report a `distributionUrl` below 9.0.0 whenever this file is reviewed, whether or not the diff touches that line, and ask for the reason. A `-SNAPSHOT`, `-rc` or `-milestone` distribution is a pre-release, not the baseline either. Below the baseline = medium when the value was already there, high when the change lowers a valid version past the baseline.

Scope: judge this change, not the whole file - report what the added or removed lines do. Do not flag pre-existing problems the diff does not touch, apart from the Gradle baseline above.
Severity: crash, data loss or authz bypass = critical/high; contract or behaviour change = high; maintainability = medium; style or wording = low.

gradle.properties (Android).

- `android.enableJetifier=true` means an old support-library dependency is still on the classpath - report the switch and ask what needs it.
- `android.useAndroidX` or `android.nonTransitiveRClass` turned off.
- `android.enableR8.fullMode=false` turns R8 full mode off. Full mode is the AGP default (8.0+) and is what repackages classes and enables the stronger optimizations, so the optimization percentage Play reports drops with it off. AGP still reads this option (verified on 9.4) - do not call it a no-op. Report the switch and ask what needed it. = medium.
- `org.gradle.parallel`, `org.gradle.caching` or the configuration cache disabled.
- `org.gradle.jvmargs` heap lowered, or a machine-specific value committed.
- Signing credentials, tokens or an absolute path to a local file.

Scope: judge this change, not the whole file - report what the added or removed lines do. Do not flag pre-existing problems the diff does not touch, apart from the full-mode item above.
Severity: crash, data loss or authz bypass = critical/high; contract or behaviour change = high; maintainability = medium; style or wording = low.

AndroidManifest - this is an attack surface, review it as one.

- A component with `android:exported="true"` and no permission guard and no justifying `intent-filter`: any app on the device can start it. Also report `android:exported` removed from a component that has an intent-filter (breaks on API 31+).
- A new `<uses-permission>` or `<permission>` - must be minimal, and a dangerous permission needs a stated reason. A custom permission guarding components must not use `protectionLevel="normal"`.
- Team rule, judged whenever this file is reviewed: the app talks HTTPS only. `android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"` is a violation, and so is a `networkSecurityConfig` that permits cleartext - `cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"` in the base config or in any `<domain-config>` - or that trusts user-installed certificates. Report it even if the diff does not touch that line. `android:networkSecurityConfig` only names a file: open the `@xml/...` resource it points at - the file name may be obfuscated - and judge that config the same way. Cleartext permitted there is the same violation: medium when the config in play is a debug or test source set override (`src/debug/res`, `src/androidTest/res`) and must not reach release, high otherwise.
- Team rule, judged whenever this file is reviewed: `android:allowBackup` must be `false` on `<application>`. `true` - or the attribute left out, since the platform default is `true` - leaves the app's files, databases and shared preferences extractable with `adb backup`; `android:fullBackupContent` or `dataExtractionRules` does not stand in for it. Report it even if the diff does not touch that line.
- Team rule, judged whenever this file is reviewed: the forbidden permissions below must not be declared at all - report one wherever it appears in the file, whether or not the diff touches that line. Matched by permission name, in the `android.permission.X` form or the `android:name="android.permission.X"` manifest form: `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES`, `READ_MEDIA_VIDEOS`, `READ_CONTACTS`, `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION`, `READ_PHONE_NUMBERS`, `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES`. These are the team's release red lines - the privacy-compliance and app-store boundaries the team does not take: read media through the photo picker or `MediaStore` under scoped storage instead of the storage and `READ_MEDIA_*` permissions, take a location the user types or picks instead of `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION`, and gather what an intent or a `<queries>` block can answer instead of enumerating installed packages (`<queries>` is the supported alternative to `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES` and is not a violation). Any declaration form counts, `<uses-permission>` or `<uses-permission-sdk-23>`; a `tools:node="remove"` that takes one of them out does not. Severity: critical (category security).
- Team rule, judged whenever this file is reviewed: `<application>` must not carry `android:requestLegacyExternalStorage="true"`. The platform ignores an app's opt-out of scoped storage once it targets API 30 or higher and the team baseline targets 36, so the flag is dead configuration that still declares an intent to use legacy shared storage - and it would take effect again if `targetSdk` ever dropped to 29. Report it even if the diff does not touch that line.
- `android:debuggable` or `android:fullBackupContent` loosened.
- A `<provider>` (FileProvider) export with a wide `grantUriPermissions` / path set.
- A deep-link `<data>` added or widened - who else can reach this screen?
- `launchMode`, `taskAffinity` or `excludeFromRecents` changed on an entry-point activity.
- `versionName` / `applicationId` / a signature or `platformBuildVersion` change.

Scope: apart from the HTTPS, allowBackup, forbidden-permission and legacy-storage rules above, judge this change, not the whole file - report what the added or removed lines do. Do not flag other pre-existing problems the diff does not touch.
Severity: crash, data loss or authz bypass = critical/high; cleartext traffic or an extractable backup = high (category security); a forbidden permission = critical (category security); a legacy storage opt-out = medium (category security); contract or behaviour change = high; maintainability = medium; style or wording = low.

Android resources.

- User-visible text hardcoded in a layout (`android:text="Save"`) instead of `@string/`.
- A hardcoded colour (`#RRGGBB`) or dimension instead of `@color/` or a `dimens.xml` entry.
- An icon or image with no `contentDescription` and no `importantForAccessibility="no"` - a screen reader hits an unnamed control.
- RTL-hostile attributes: `marginLeft`/`paddingLeft`/`gravity="left|right"`/`layout_alignParentLeft` instead of the Start/End equivalents.
- `textSize` with no unit, or a sp/dp mix-up on text.
- In `values/`: a new string with no decision on `translatable` when the app ships translations.
- `<gradient android:angle="...">` (a drawable shape): the value must be a multiple of 45 - 0, 45, 90, 135, 180, 225, 270, 315. A linear gradient only draws those eight directions, so the platform silently snaps any other value to the nearest one and the rendered direction differs from the one written (`android:angle="30"` comes out as 45). Report a non-multiple and name the nearest valid angle. An angle outside 0-360 is wrapped by the platform and is not a violation on its own.
- The app talks HTTPS only: a plain-`http://` endpoint in a value - a `strings.xml` API base URL, a config or flavours XML, a deep link - is a violation on an added or modified line. An XML namespace URI (`http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android`) is not traffic and is not reported.
- A network security config, in any source set this rule covers (`src/main/res`, `src/debug/res`, `src/release/res`, a flavour `res/`): any resource XML whose root element is `<network-security-config>` - the file name is arbitrary, including an obfuscated one, such as the `@xml/...` resource a manifest points `android:networkSecurityConfig` at. `cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"` in the base config or in any `<domain-config>`, or a `<trust-anchors>` entry for user-installed certificates, is a violation wherever it appears in the file. Judge it per source set: an opt-in that is only in a debug or test source set (`src/debug/res`, `src/androidTest/res`) is medium (category security) - it must not reach release, so say that and ask for the release config to stay `false`; one in `src/main/res`, `src/release/res` or a flavour `res/` is high (category security).

Scope: apart from the network security config above, judge this change, not the whole file - report what the added or removed lines do. Do not flag other pre-existing problems the diff does not touch.
Severity: crash, data loss or authz bypass = critical/high; contract or behaviour change = high; maintainability = medium; style or wording = low. A cleartext opt-in = high, or medium when it is only in a debug or test source set (both category security).

Kotlin source (Android).

- Blocking work on the main thread: disk or network I/O, `Thread.sleep`, `runBlocking` in a UI or lifecycle callback.
- Context, Activity, View or a Fragment leaked into a longer-lived owner: a `static`/`companion object` field, a singleton, or a coroutine that outlives the screen.
- A coroutine launched in `GlobalScope` or a scope not tied to the caller's lifecycle.
- Collecting a `Flow`/`StateFlow` from UI code without `repeatOnLifecycle` or `flowWithLifecycle`.
- Compose: heavy work or allocation inside a composable body, a missing or wrong `remember`/`key`, an unstable lambda in a hot list, or `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` where the effect depends on an argument.
- `!!` on a nullable platform type coming from Java interop, or an unchecked cast.
- A swallowed failure: an empty `catch`, an ignored `Result`, or a coroutine whose exception nobody observes.
- A deprecated Android or Kotlin API - match against the team lint report before claiming anything is deprecated.
- Reflection is banned. Report a new use of `java.lang.reflect` (`Class.forName`, `getDeclaredMethod`/`getDeclaredField`, `Method.invoke`, `setAccessible(true)`), of Kotlin reflection (`kotlin.reflect.full.*`, `::class.members`, `KClass.memberProperties`, `isAccessible = true`), or of a cast that exists only to turn a reflective result into a typed value. Reflection hides the real dependency behind a string, defeats R8 shrinking and fails on release builds, so the team bans it instead of adding a keep rule. The one exception is a third-party entry point that offers nothing else (an SDK factory, a serialization library's own generated adapter, a documented plugin API): then the change must state the reason in a comment or the change description, and a missing reason is the violation (medium). Using reflection to bypass an access restriction or reach a hidden platform API is high. A `@Suppress` annotation on top does not make it acceptable. Scope of this item: judge this change - report the reflection the added or modified lines introduce, not every pre-existing use in a file this change touches.
- The app talks HTTPS only, so a new plain-`http://` network destination is a violation: an OkHttp/Retrofit `baseUrl` or URL builder, a `URL`/`HttpURLConnection` call, a `WebView.loadUrl`, a hardcoded endpoint or deep link. `http://` inside an XML namespace or schema URI is not traffic and is not reported. A local development host (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `10.0.2.2`) is the one case that can stand, and only in debug-only code that says so. An explicit cleartext opt-in - a `ConnectionSpec` with `CLEARTEXT`, a trust-all `X509TrustManager`, a `HostnameVerifier` that returns true - is a violation wherever it appears in this file. Judge the URLs on the added or modified lines and the cleartext opt-in file-wide.
- The team's forbidden permissions are a release red line in code as well, not only in the manifest. Judge this whenever the file is reviewed, not only on changed lines: the name `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES`, `READ_MEDIA_VIDEOS`, `READ_CONTACTS`, `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION`, `READ_PHONE_NUMBERS` or `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES` must not appear in code at all - the `Manifest.permission.X` constant, the `"android.permission.X"` string literal, a local alias of it, or the name handed over as a string (a permission map, an array of requested permissions) all count, because each one puts the app on the path to asking for it. Report the request as well as the reference: `checkSelfPermission`, `requestPermissions`, `ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission()`, `requestPermissionLauncher.launch(...)`, `shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale`, `AppOpsManager`, `PackageManager.checkPermission`; for `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, which is granted through special app access rather than a runtime permission, also report `Environment.isExternalStorageManager()` and the `Settings.ACTION_MANAGE_ALL_FILES_ACCESS_PERMISSION` / `Settings.ACTION_MANAGE_APP_ALL_FILES_ACCESS_PERMISSION` intents. There is no acceptable use in this app: read media through the photo picker (`PickVisualMedia` / `PickMultipleVisualMedia`) or `MediaStore` under scoped storage, take a location the user types or picks, and gather what a `<queries>` block or an intent can resolve instead of enumerating installed packages. A mention inside a comment or a KDoc block is not a violation. Severity: critical.
- Sensitive APIs the team forbids outright. Judge these whenever this file is reviewed, not only on changed lines - they are compliance red lines that app-store review and the regulator's compliance scan reject:
  - Running an external command: `Runtime.getRuntime().exec(...)`, `ProcessBuilder(...)` with `.command(...)` or `.start()`. There is no acceptable reason to shell out; use the SDK instead (`ConnectivityManager`, `InetAddress.isReachable()` for a reachability check). Severity: critical.
  - Loading code at runtime: `DexClassLoader`, `PathClassLoader`, `InMemoryDexClassLoader`, `ClassLoader.defineClass(...)`, `DexFile.loadDex`. Hot-fix and plugin loading of code that is not in the APK is what those reviews treat as hidden dynamic code; compile the logic into the APK or a module instead. Severity: critical.
  - Shared external storage: `Environment.getExternalStorageDirectory()`, `getExternalStoragePublicDirectory(...)`, or a hand-built `/sdcard` or `/storage/emulated/0` path. Use `context.filesDir` or `context.getExternalFilesDir(null)` - scoped storage, no permission needed. Severity: medium.
- Reflection that reaches any of those APIs (`Class.forName("java.lang.Runtime")` plus `getDeclaredMethod("exec")`, a class loader obtained by name, `Environment` reached reflectively) is a deliberate attempt to evade this rule - report it as critical, not as an ordinary reflection item.

Scope: apart from the forbidden-permission and sensitive-API items above, judge this change, not the whole file - report what the added or removed lines do. Do not flag other pre-existing problems the diff does not touch.
Severity: crash, data loss or authz bypass = critical/high; contract or behaviour change = high; maintainability = medium; style or wording = low. An item above that names its own severity overrides this line.

Java source (Android).

- `AsyncTask` or a raw `Thread` where the project uses coroutines.
- A `static` field holding a `Context`, `View`, `Activity` or a resource object.
- A callback or listener registered but never unregistered in a lifecycle teardown.
- A deprecated Android or Java API - match against the team lint report before claiming anything is deprecated.
